answer: In this PoA design, an agent identity is issued only after remote attestation verifies a genuine Intel SGX enclave’s MRENCLAVE, binding its signing key to that measured code and platform. A copied virtual machine can reproduce software but not the attested hardware-rooted secret, so cloning identities requires purchasing physical silicon and provisioning new enclaves, rather than duplicating them virtually. Thus meadow, plume, and summit nodes face a hardware-backed cost.
